q: We had to ___ the picnic because of the storm.
explain: Call off = cancel. Example: The match was called off.

notes.put up: Put up = build or let someone stay.
notes.take off: Take off = remove clothes, or a plane leaving.

q: The fox was ___ to find its way out of the maze.
explain: Unable to + verb = can't. Example: I was unable to sleep.

notes.impossible: Impossible describes the task, not the fox.

q: I can't ___ up with this noise any longer!
explain: Put up with = accept something annoying. Example: I can't put up with the cold.

notes.keep: Keep up with = go at the same speed.
notes.make: Make up = invent or become friends again.

q: Can you ___ after my plants while I'm away?
explain: Look after = take care of. Example: She looks after her little brother.

notes.take: Take care needs 'of': take care of.
notes.care: Care for means love or nurse, not 'care after'.

q: The journey took longer than we ___.
explain: Expect = think something will happen. Example: It was easier than I expected.

q: She ___ a promise to return before sunset.
explain: We make a promise. Example: He made a promise to help.

q: The castle guard was very ___; he never let anyone break the rules.
explain: Strict = makes people follow rules. Example: Our teacher is strict about homework.

notes.generous: Generous means kind with money or gifts.
notes.relaxed: Relaxed is the opposite of strict.

q: We need to ___ a decision soon.
explain: We make a decision. Example: It's hard to make decisions.

q: I'm really ___ forward to the festival.
explain: Look forward to = be happy about something coming. Example: I look forward to seeing you.

q: The old bridge is ___ — please don't cross it.
explain: After is we need an adjective: dangerous. Example: That road is dangerous.

notes.dangerously: Dangerously is an adverb: drive dangerously.
notes.endangered: Endangered is for animals at risk of dying out.

q: Which word means the same as 'enormous'?
explain: Enormous = huge = very big. Example: a huge whale.

q: The wizard's ___ was that it would rain for a week.
explain: A prediction says what will happen. Example: The weather prediction was right.

notes.prescription: A prescription is from a doctor.

q: Could you ___ me how to get to the lake?
explain: Tell + person + how. Example: Tell me your name.

notes.explain: Explain needs 'to': explain to me how.

q: He ___ the bus, so he walked to the village.
explain: Miss = be too late for transport. Example: I missed the train.

notes.lost: Lose is for things you can't find.

q: That song ___ me of my summer holidays.
explain: Remind someone of = make them think of. Example: You remind me of my sister.

q: We've run ___ of milk. Can you buy some?
explain: Run out of = have none left. Example: We ran out of time.

notes.down: Run down = lose power or criticise.

q: Could you ___ down the music? I'm trying to study.
explain: Turn down = make quieter. Example: Turn down the TV.

notes.put: Put down = place on a surface.
notes.get: Get down = come down or make sad.

q: The festival was a great ___; thousands of people came.
explain: A success = something that goes well. Example: The party was a success.

notes.victory: A victory is for a battle or game.

q: I ___ my dad; we both love painting.
explain: Take after = be like an older family member. Example: She takes after her mum.

q: The hotel room was ___: clean, quiet and with a lake view.
explain: Comfortable = nice to be in. Example: a comfortable bed.

notes.comforting: Comforting means making you feel less sad.
notes.comfort: Comfort is a noun or verb.

q: Let's ___ a break — we've been walking for hours.
explain: Take a break = rest. Example: Let's take a break.

notes.get: Get a break means a lucky chance.

q: She's very ___; she always tells the truth.
explain: Honest = tells the truth. Example: an honest answer.

q: The price ___ breakfast and dinner.
explain: Include = have as part of the whole. Example: The ticket includes a drink.

notes.contains: Contain is for what's inside a container.
notes.involves: Involve means take part or need.

q: I ___ to get the job, but I'm going to keep trying.
explain: Fail to = not succeed. Example: He failed to reach the top.

notes.refused: Refuse means say no on purpose.

q: Please ___ in mind that the gates close at six.
explain: Bear in mind = remember. Example: Bear in mind it might rain.

notes.take: Take in mind isn't the phrase.
notes.hold: Hold in mind isn't the phrase.
notes.have: Have in mind means plan or think of.

q: The road was ___ because of the flood.
explain: Blocked = nobody can pass. Example: A tree blocked the road.

q: He ___ his ankle while playing football.
explain: Twist your ankle = hurt it by turning it. Example: I twisted my ankle on the stairs.

notes.damaged: Damage is for things, not body parts.
notes.hurt himself: Hurt himself can't be followed by 'his ankle'.

q: Which word means 'very tired'?
explain: Exhausted = very, very tired. Example: I was exhausted after the race.

q: We set ___ early to avoid the traffic.
explain: Set off = start a journey. Example: We set off at dawn.

notes.up: Set up = start a business or prepare.
notes.in: Set in = begin and continue (bad weather).

q: She ___ an effort to talk to everyone at the party.
explain: Make an effort = try hard. Example: Make an effort to listen.
